environment.language: Original analysis is Stata (.do files reading .dta). Stata is proprietary and is NOT installed in this workspace, so the shipped code paths cannot execute directly. Faithfully reimplement the shipped regressions in Python (pandas can read the .dta inputs; linearmodels provides weighted 2SLS with cluster-robust SEs that match Stata's `ivregress 2sls [aw=...], cluster(statefip)`). R (haven + fixest/AER) is an acceptable alternative.
environment.setup_hints: pip install pandas numpy scipy linearmodels statsmodels openpyxl. No GPU is needed — this is small-N commuting-zone econometrics (722 CZs x 2 periods); the RTX A6000s are irrelevant. Work on the writable copy at /workspace/output/replication/codebase/. All inputs are pre-built .dta files in dta/ (workfile_china.dta is the basis for Tables 3-10 and App Tables 1/4/5; workfile_china_preperiod.dta for Table 2; workfile_china_long.dta for Figure 2; import_levels.dta/export_levels.dta for Table 1; figure1_data.dta for Figure 1). CRITICAL matching notes when reimplementing: (1) use analytic weights `timepwt48` for all regressions unless the do-file uses `l_popcount`; (2) cluster standard errors on `statefip`; (3) endogenous regressor is `d_tradeusch_pw` instrumented by `d_tradeotch_pw_lag`; (4) controls entering the fully-controlled spec are `l_shind_manuf_cbp l_sh_popedu_c l_sh_popfborn l_sh_empl_f l_sh_routine33 l_task_outsource reg* t2` (reg* = Census-division dummies, t2 = period dummy); (5) apply Stata's small-sample cluster adjustment so SEs line up. Do NOT read the shipped log/*.scsv or tab-fig/*.xls result artifacts as answers — regenerate every number by running the regressions.

steps.description: Set up the environment and validate inputs. Copy the repo to the working dir, install the Python dependencies, then load each .dta with pandas.read_stata and confirm the variables used by the do-files exist (e.g. in workfile_china.dta: d_sh_empl_mfg, d_tradeusch_pw, d_tradeotch_pw_lag, timepwt48, statefip, l_shind_manuf_cbp, l_sh_popedu_c, l_sh_popfborn, l_sh_empl_f, l_sh_routine33, l_task_outsource, reg* dummies, t2; N should be 1444 = 722 CZs x 2 periods). Write a small helper module implementing weighted 2SLS with state-clustered SEs (linearmodels.IV2SLS) to be reused by later steps.
steps.command_hint: cp -r /workspace/repo /workspace/output/replication/codebase && cd /workspace/output/replication/codebase && pip install pandas numpy scipy linearmodels statsmodels openpyxl && python -c "import pandas as pd; df=pd.read_stata('dta/workfile_china.dta'); print(df.shape); print([c for c in df.columns][:50])"
steps.expected_outcome: Prints the shape of workfile_china.dta (N rows ~1444, wide column set) and a variable manifest confirming the endogenous var, instrument, weight, cluster and control variables are present. A reusable helper (e.g. codebase/repro/iv.py) is created. No claim values produced.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 3 (headline manufacturing-employment-share 2SLS). Reimplement czone_analysis_ipw_final.do lines 119-126: six IV2SLS specifications of d_sh_empl_mfg on the instrumented d_tradeusch_pw, adding controls cumulatively (col1: t2 only; col2: + l_shind_manuf_cbp; col3: + reg*; col4: + edu/fborn/female; col5: + routine/outsource; col6: fully controlled), all weighted by timepwt48 and clustered on statefip. Emit the coefficient and SE on d_tradeusch_pw for all six columns. The col-6 estimate is the paper's headline; the col-2 coefficient scaled by the 2000-2007 interquartile exposure range (~1.06, from Appendix Table 1 in step 7) gives the 75th-vs-25th differential of claim C27.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table3.csv with one row per specification (col1..col6) and columns {coef_d_tradeusch_pw, se, first_stage_coef}. Six 2SLS coefficients (all negative, monotone-ish) plus the fully-controlled column's coef and SE. Also prints the col-2 coefficient used for the interquartile differential.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 4 (population) and Table 5 (employment/unemployment/non-employment). From czone_analysis_ipw_final.do: Table 4 (L133-152) regresses lnchg_popworkage and its education/age subgroups on instrumented import exposure (report the fully-controlled row); Table 5 panel A (L170-174) regresses log employment-count outcomes lnchg_no_empl_mfg / lnchg_no_empl_nmfg / lnchg_no_unempl / lnchg_no_nilf / lnchg_no_ssadiswkrs; panel B (L175-187) regresses the population-share outcomes d_sh_empl_mfg / d_sh_empl_nmfg / d_sh_unempl / d_sh_nilf / d_sh_ssadiswkrs and their edu_c/edu_nc splits; and L165-167 give the overall net employment rate d_sh_empl for all / college / noncollege. All fully-controlled, weighted, clustered on statefip. The differential fall in manufacturing employees and the emp/pop change (interquartile-scaled) are the employment axes of headline claim C7.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table4_pop.csv (rows = pop outcomes incl edu/age subgroups; columns {coef, se}) and outputs/table5_emp.csv (rows = count outcomes [panel A] and share outcomes [panel B] incl edu_c/edu_nc, plus d_sh_empl overall/college/noncollege; columns {coef, se}). Manufacturing-share coefficient matches the Table 3 col-6 headline; population coefficient is small and insignificant.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 6 (wage changes) and Table 7 (manufacturing vs non-manufacturing). From czone_analysis_ipw_final.do: Table 6 (L196-205) regresses d_avg_lnwkwage and its male/female and college/noncollege splits on instrumented import exposure; Table 7 (L213-226) regresses log employment counts and average log weekly wages separately for manufacturing (d_avg_lnwkwage_mfg) and non-manufacturing (d_avg_lnwkwage_nmfg). All fully-controlled, weighted by timepwt48, clustered on statefip. The mean-weekly-earnings decline is the earnings axis of headline claim C7.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table6_wage.csv (rows = all/male/female x overall/college/noncollege; columns {coef, se}) and outputs/table7_mfgnmfg.csv (rows = mfg/nmfg employment-count and wage outcomes; columns {coef, se}). The overall wage coefficient is negative; the manufacturing-wage coefficient is small and insignificant while the non-manufacturing-wage coefficient is negative and significant.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 8 (transfer receipts) and Table 9 (household income per capita). From czone_analysis_ipw_final.do: Table 8 (L234-252) regresses log-change and level-change per-capita transfer outcomes (lnchg_trans_totindiv_pc, lnchg_trans_taaimp_pc [Trade Adjustment Assistance], lnchg_trans_ssaret_pc, lnchg_trans_ssadis_pc [SSA disability], lnchg_trans_totmed_pc [medical], lnchg_trans_unemp_pc, lnchg_trans_fedinc_pc, and the corresponding d_trans_*_pc dollar levels) on instrumented import exposure; Table 9 (L260-273) regresses relchg_/d_ household-income-per-capita outcomes (avg_hhincsum_pc_pw total, avg_hhincwage_pc_pw wage/salary, avg_hhinctrans_pc_pw social-security+AFDC). All fully-controlled, weighted, clustered on statefip. Per-capita transfer increases are the transfer axis of headline claim C7.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table8_trans.csv (rows = per-capita transfer categories in both log-change and dollar-level form; columns {coef, se}) and outputs/table9_hhinc.csv (rows = total / wage-salary / transfer household income in relative-change and dollar-level form; columns {coef, se}). Total-transfer coefficient positive; TAA has the largest proportionate coefficient; wage/salary and total household income coefficients negative.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 10 (alternative trade-exposure measures) for the manufacturing employment share. From czone_analysis_ipw_final.do: the gross baseline is Table 3 col-6 (-0.60 comparator); then re-estimate d_sh_empl_mfg with (a) domestic+international exposure d_tradex_usch_pw instrumented by d_tradex_otch_pw_lag (L284), (b) net-of-intermediate-inputs d_tradeusch_netinput_pw with instruments d_tradeotch_pw_lag + d_inputotch_pw_lag (L297), (c) net imports d_netimpusch_pw with instruments d_tradeotch_pw_lag + d_expotch_pw_lag (L310), (d) gravity-residual reduced-form OLS on d_traderes_pw_lag (L323), and (e) factor content of net imports d_nettradefactor_usch_io (L336). All fully-controlled, weighted, clustered on statefip.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table10_altexposure.csv with one row per exposure measure {gross_baseline, dom_intl, net_intermediates, net_imports, gravity_residual, factor_content} and columns {coef_on_exposure, se} for the d_sh_empl_mfg outcome. All coefficients negative and of broadly similar magnitude.

steps.description: Reproduce Appendix Table 1 descriptives and the Appendix Table 4 OLS estimate. From czone_analysis_ipw_final.do: (a) summarize d_tradeusch_pw by year weighted by timepwt48 with detail (L31-32) to obtain the median ten-year-equivalent Chinese import growth per worker in the 1990s (yr==1990) and 2000s (yr==2000) and the 25th/75th percentiles (claim C24); (b) Appendix Table 4 (L383) OLS of d_sh_empl_mfg on d_tradeusch_pw with the full control set, weighted, clustered on statefip — the preferred-specification OLS estimate (claim C8; note the lagged-employment-weight variant of C8 is not shipped and is recorded under claim_coverage).
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/apptab1_importgrowth.csv (rows = year 1990/2000; columns {p25, p50, p75} of d_tradeusch_pw) and outputs/apptab4_ols.csv with the OLS coefficient and SE on d_tradeusch_pw for the fully-controlled manufacturing-share regression. OLS coefficient negative and smaller in magnitude than the 2SLS estimate.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 2 (2SLS by period) and the falsification test. Reimplement czone_analysis_preperiod_final.do on workfile_china_preperiod.dta: regress d_sh_empl_mfg on instrumented d_tradeusch_pw for 1990-2000 (yr==1990), 2000-2007 (yr==2000), and the stacked 1990-2007 (yr>=1990 with time dummy t2000) — claim C3; then the falsification test regressing pre-period manufacturing-employment change on FUTURE import exposure (d_tradeusch_pw_future instrumented by d_tradeotch_pw_lag_future) for 1970-1980 (yr==1970), 1980-1990 (yr==1980), and stacked 1970-1990 (t1980) — claim C4. All weighted by timepwt48, clustered on statefip.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table2_byperiod.csv with rows {1990-2000, 2000-2007, stacked_1990-2007, falsification_1970-1980, falsification_1980-1990, falsification_stacked_1970-1990} and columns {coef, se}. Contemporaneous coefficients negative and significant; falsification (future-exposure) coefficients small and insignificant.

steps.description: Reproduce the Figure 2 first-stage and reduced-form regressions. Reimplement czone_plot_import_long_final.do on workfile_china_long.dta: (a) first stage — regress d_tradeusch_pw on d_tradeotch_pw_lag with control l_shind_manuf_cbp, weighted by timepwt48, clustered on statefip (L28), reporting the coefficient, robust SE, and t-stat on the instrument; (b) reduced form — regress d_pct_manuf on d_tradeotch_pw_lag with the same control/weight/cluster (L42). Optionally regenerate the added-variable plots (partialling out l_shind_manuf_cbp) as PNGs mirroring the two shipped .gph files.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/figure2_firststage_reducedform.csv with rows {first_stage, reduced_form} and columns {coef_on_instrument, robust_se, t_stat}. First-stage coefficient positive with large t; reduced-form coefficient negative. Optionally writes outputs/fig2_firststage_av.png and outputs/fig2_reducedform_av.png showing a positive-slope first-stage and negative-slope reduced-form added-variable scatter.

steps.description: Reproduce Table 1 trade statistics and the Figure 1 time series. (a) Reimplement import_stats_final.do on import_levels.dta / export_levels.dta: summarize l_totimp_{usch,uslw,...}_{1991,2000,2007} and l_totexp_{usch,otch}_{1992,2000,2007} to obtain US imports-from-China and exports-to-China levels and growth 1991-2007, plus China's share of US manufacturing imports from low-income countries (usch relative to the low-income aggregate) in 1991 and 2007 (claim C22). (b) Load figure1_data.dta and read the China import-penetration series (impr) and manufacturing-employment/population series (cpsman) for 1991 and 2007 (claim C23); optionally regenerate figure1.png.
steps.expected_outcome: Writes outputs/table1_trade.csv (rows = US imports-from-China, exports-to-China, China share of low-income mfg imports; columns for years 1991/1992, 2000, 2007 and a growth column) and outputs/figure1_series.csv (rows = year; columns {import_penetration_impr, mfg_emp_pop_cpsman}). Import growth far exceeds export growth; China's import share rises; the mfg emp/pop series declines while penetration rises.

claim_coverage.reason: Headline aggregate counterfactual (% of national mfg-employment decline explained). No shipped do-file computes this decomposition; it is a hand calculation in the paper text/Excel combining Table 2 coefficients with national employment aggregates. Building-block coefficients are produced (step 8) but the % figures are not emitted by any code path.
Supply-driven (48%) counterfactual worker-count decomposition (548k/982k). No shipped script computes it; derived in text from the estimates and aggregate employment, not produced by the do-files.

Appendix robustness dropping specific industries (steel/glass/cement, computers, apparel). Requires rebuilding the CZ import-exposure variable from sic87dd_trade_data excluding industries; the exposure-construction code is not shipped (only the pre-built workfile), so this robustness variant cannot be run. Appendix-only, deprioritized.

Deadweight-loss-of-transfers welfare calculation ($13/$21; $22-44 range) applying a 40% marginal excess burden. No shipped code computes this; it is a text-level calculation on top of the Table 8 transfer estimates.
Deadweight-loss-of-nonparticipation welfare calculation ($43/$69; $87-137 range). No shipped code path; text-level welfare arithmetic on the Table 5 nonparticipation estimates.
External cited statistics (China's ~3/4 share of LMIC manufacturing-VA growth; 8.0% vs 3.9% TFP growth) drawn from Brandt et al. and BLS, not from this replication package's data or code.

The distinctive number ($113.18, SE 41.53) is a re-estimate normalizing transfers by total workers rather than residents; no shipped do-file runs this re-normalization. The $58 residents-normalized point estimate it references is already produced in step 5 (Table 8).
